mobile.title: Mobile
mobile.description: View and continue your sessions from the Pi mx Remote phone app on the same local network. Connections are end-to-end encrypted and never pass through a server.
mobile.portInUse: Port {{port}} is already in use. Pick another port.
mobile.portDesc: Port phones use to reach this computer.
mobile.noAddress: No local network address found. Check that this computer is on Wi‑Fi or Ethernet.
mobile.addressesDesc: Away from this network, the phone can connect over Tailscale, ZeroTier or WireGuard when both devices are in the same overlay network.
mobile.pairingDesc: Scan the code with the phone app to pair. On Windows, allow pi Desktop on private networks in the firewall.
mobile.ephemeralKey: OS encryption is unavailable, so the host key lives in memory only; phones must pair again after a restart.
mobile.wideAreaDesc: Connect from outside your Wi-Fi: run a tunnel or forward the port. Traffic is always wss, and the phone remembers this certificate's fingerprint from pairing.
mobile.certificateDesc: Valid until {{expires}}, covers {{names}} addresses. The phone recognises this desktop by fingerprint, not through a public CA.
mobile.certificateOff: No certificate while the gateway is stopped.
mobile.regenerateTlsHint: Only for a new machine or a lost certificate: every phone has to scan the QR again afterwards.
mobile.publicHostsDesc: Tunnel hostnames or a forwarded domain:port. They go into the QR, so the phone can fall back to them when away from home.
mobile.tunnelHint: Tunnel example: cloudflared tunnel --url https://127.0.0.1:{{port}} --no-tls-verify, then add the hostname it prints.
mobile.projectsDesc: Phones see the same project list as this desktop — no per-project approval.
mobile.projectsShared: Projects you open later appear on the phone automatically; to limit what the phone sees, change the project list on this desktop.
mobile.relayDesc: Your own relay server: the desktop dials out, the phone comes in from any network. No cloudflared / frp, and the phone never needs a VPN. The relay only moves bytes — content stays end-to-end encrypted.
mobile.relayUrlDesc: host:port of your server (pick a region near you for the lowest latency).
mobile.relayTokenDesc: Must match the server's --token; without it nobody can attach a desktop.
mobile.relayHint: Deploy with: node scripts/relay/server.mjs --port 8443 --token <token>, behind caddy / nginx for the certificate. If the desktop runs a VPN, add the relay host to its bypass list — otherwise this machine reaches the relay the long way around and latency gets worse.
mobile.relayInvalid: That address does not parse: use host or host:port.
mobile.relayProbeFailed: Could not read a certificate: check the address/port and that the relay is running.
mobile.relayWizardDesc: When someone else wants their phone to reach their own desktop, they run one command on their own server.
mobile.relayStep1: Get a small server with a public IP (any 1 vCPU / 1 GB box is enough) and log in as root.
mobile.relayStep2: Generate a token, copy the command below onto that server; it installs the service, enables it on boot, mints a certificate and prints the address / token / fingerprint.
mobile.relayStep3: Open the same port in the cloud firewall (security group); then fill the address and token here, click Check certificate → Trust & save, and re-scan the pairing QR on the phone.
mobile.relayCommandHint: Click Generate token first — the paste-ready command shows up here.
mobile.relayWizardNote: The token is shown only here; keep it somewhere safe. It is the same value as the Token field above.

purge.description: Takes over pi's system prompt: once enabled, the next message in this session runs on your local persona instead of pi's built-in identity and refusal wording. Prompt-only — the app itself is not patched.
purge.enableHint: The switch writes config.json; the extension re-reads it before every request, so it applies to the next message in this session without a restart.

modeHint.strict: strict: persona + working directory only, the host prompt is dropped. Strongest, but AGENTS.md / skills list go with it.
modeHint.replace: replace: persona first, host prompt without its identity line and <docs> block; tool rules stay. Good default.
modeHint.append: append: persona prepended, host prompt untouched. Mildest.

modeCompare.strict: Persona + cwd only; the host prompt is dropped entirely (AGENTS.md and the skills list too)
modeCompare.replace: Persona first; identity and doc sections of the host prompt are cut, tool rules kept
modeCompare.append: Persona prepended to the host prompt; the host prompt is untouched

purge.personaHint: The persona file is the prompt itself. The installer ships the one you use in DSH; you can swap in your own markdown.
purge.configHint: Shared state between the extension and this page
purge.needReinstall: The extension is not in the agent directory yet: press "Reinstall", then restart Pi mx once.
purge.needPersona: This installer ships a persona but it is not in the agent dir yet: press "Reinstall".
purge.needPersonaNoBundle: This installer does not include a persona (it was not generated at build time): use "Import persona", or drop persona.md next to the app executable and press "Reinstall".
purge.footer: State lives in ~/.pi/agent/purge/config.json and survives quitting the app. To restore stock behaviour, turn this off and delete extensions/pi-app-purge.ts.

promptInject.title: Prompt injection
promptInject.description: Write your own prompt block into APPEND_SYSTEM.md. Only the marked block is touched; anything else in the file is kept, and every write can be reverted.
promptInject.enableDesc: On writes the marked block into the target file; off removes it. Takes effect in new sessions.
promptInject.scopeDesc: Global writes to ~/.pi/agent/APPEND_SYSTEM.md; project writes to <project>/.pi/APPEND_SYSTEM.md.
promptInject.revealed: Shown in folder (this file can't be opened directly)
promptInject.noProject: No open project, project-level write is unavailable
promptInject.otherContentDesc: Content outside the marked block is never modified, and survives a revert.
promptInject.textPlaceholder: Text to append to the system prompt…
promptInject.textHint: Written as a marked block, so your hand-written parts stay intact.
promptInject.noBackups: No backups yet. One is taken before every write.
promptInject.applied: Written; takes effect in a new session
promptInject.reverted: Reverted; the marked block was removed

imageGen.title: Image generation
imageGen.description: Generate images through the app itself: your local ChatGPT/Codex subscription auth, or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint. With this on, the agent uses the built-in image_gen tool instead of an MCP image server.
imageGen.providerHint: Subscription uses chatgpt.com's Codex image endpoint (with browser-fingerprint headers, which avoids the silent downgrade); custom calls your /v1/images/generations.
imageGen.authHint: Reuses ~/.codex/auth.json, so signing in through Codex or the DSH ChatGPT login plugin is enough.
imageGen.modelHintCodex: Leave empty for the subscription default (gpt-image-2.6); 2.6 / 2.5 / 2 all work. Use Sync models to pull the account list.
imageGen.modelHintCustom: Type any model your endpoint supports, e.g. gpt-image-1.5 / Nano-banana. Suggestions only.
imageGen.baseUrlHint: OpenAI-compatible root, e.g. https://host/v1 (/images/generations is appended).
imageGen.apiKeyHint: Stored only in the local pi-desktop.json, never inside the project.
imageGen.sizeHint: auto lets the service decide; the subscription endpoint may change the actual size.
imageGen.qualityHint: auto is the cheapest tier and a common reason for washed-out results. Default is high; try xhigh/max if your account allows it.
imageGen.identityHint: Both mimic official clients and never send a third-party marker (the old originator=pi-desktop was exactly that).
imageGen.outputDirHint: Project-relative folder, generated-images by default; the timeline shows thumbnails automatically.
imageGen.tryHint: Generate one image with the current settings to check the channel (uses quota).
imageGen.tryPlaceholder: e.g. a transparent teacup icon, clean line work
imageGen.noWorkspace: Open a project first — results are saved inside it
imageGen.promptEnhanceHint: A one-line request is auto-completed into nine aspects (subject, composition, style, palette, lighting, texture, typography, output spec, negative constraints); the result lists what was added. Turn it off to send the prompt verbatim.

lessons.description: Rules settled from your criticism live here: view, delete, add manually, and control auto-injection into every turn.
lessons.rulesDesc: These rules ride along with every message; a fresh conversation carries them from the first message.
lessons.rulesEmpty: No rules yet: worth-keeping criticism settles here automatically, or add one manually below.
lessons.optimizeDone: Polished draft filled in, review before saving
lessons.optimizeInstruction: Rewrite the settled rule below to be more precise, shorter and more actionable. Keep the meaning, do not add new requirements.
lessons.injectDesc: When on, active rules are sent to the model with every message; when off they are only kept.
lessons.lessonsDesc: {{count}} in total: raw criticism and judge reasons are view-only, never injected.
